options: a:Drivers in that lane must make the movement shown by the arrow.,b:Drivers may optionally make the movement indicated by the arrow.,c:Drivers must stop before making the movement indicated by the arrow.
note: A pavement arrow indicates the required movement for drivers in that lane; follow any traffic signals or signs before completing the turn or maneuver.

question: At a school crossing sign, how should drivers respond?
options: a:Watch for children and be prepared to stop.,b:Always stop whether there is a stop sign or not.,c:Always sound your horn when you see children.,d:Speed up to clear the area quickly.
note: Be alert for children and be ready to stop; yield to pedestrians in or about to enter crosswalks.

question: When adjusting the inside rearview mirror, what should you be able to see?
options: a:The entire rear window without moving your head.,b:Your own reflection clearly.,c:Only the road directly behind the car.,d:The passengers in the backseat only.
note: Adjust the inside mirror so you can see the entire rear window from the driver's seat by moving only your eyes, not your head.

question: What is true about driving while distracted?
options: a:It usually causes drivers to react more slowly to hazards.,b:It is never dangerous.,c:It usually causes drivers to drive faster and more safely.,d:It improves multitasking skills.
note: Distracted driving slows reaction times and increases the likelihood of a crash; it is never safe.

question: A traffic signal showing a green arrow and a red light allows you to:
options: a:Proceed only in the direction indicated by the green arrow, if the intersection is clear.,b:Go straight only and wait for a solid green to turn.,c:Ignore the arrow and follow the red light.
note: When a green arrow is displayed with a red light, you may only move in the arrow's direction, provided it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, drivers must yield the right-of-way to:
options: a:Oncoming traffic and any pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Only vehicles that signal to turn right.,c:Vehicles behind them on the same turning lane.
note: Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection when making a left turn.

question: When is it appropriate to use the parking brake?
options: a:Every time you park the vehicle.,b:Only when parking on a hill.,c:Only when stopped on a busy street.
note: Apply the parking brake each time you park, regardless of terrain or transmission type, to help prevent the vehicle from rolling.

question: What should you do before crossing railroad tracks to be safe?
options: a:Look both ways only when lights are flashing.,b:Listen, look both ways, and proceed only if it is safe.,c:Cross quickly if you see a train approaching.
note: Railroad crossings are hazardous. Look and listen for trains in both directions and obey any active warnings before proceeding.

question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?
options: a:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.,b:Slow down a little while staying in your lane.,c:Turn on hazard lights and continue driving.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection faster.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with sirens, you must pull to the side and stop to allow it to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection with a steady green light, what should you do?
options: a:Continue driving while yielding to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.,b:Stop even if the light is green.,c:Treat it as a four-way stop.
note: A green light allows you to go, but you must yield to pedestrians and traffic already in the intersection and be ready to stop if it changes.

question: What is the result of consuming alcohol while taking drugs?
options: a:It decreases the effects of the drugs and alcohol.,b:It can increase the effects of both the drugs and the alcohol.,c:It helps relieve your illness faster.
note: Combining alcohol with drugs can amplify impairment and increase risk; avoid driving if you have taken either substance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a:When entering the street from a garage, driveway, or alley.,b:Only when they are on a road to your left at an unmarked intersection.,c:Only when your signal is red.
note: You must yield when entering a public road from a driveway, garage or alley and also to pedestrians on sidewalks.

question: Which of the following best describes a defensive driver?
options: a:Easily distracted.,b:Anticipation of potential hazards and actions to avoid them.,c:Passivity toward traffic conditions.
note: Defensive drivers anticipate potential problems, maintain safe following distances, scan traffic, and take action to reduce risk.

question: What should you do when approaching an accident scene while driving?
options: a:Keep moving unless you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived.,b:Stop to look at the scene.,c:Drive slowly and block the scene for onlookers.
note: Do not stop at an accident unless you are a participant or help is needed and you are able to assist; keep moving and focus on driving to avoid creating additional hazards.

question: If you stop along the road at night, what lights should remain on?
options: a:Leave your low-beam headlights on and use emergency flashers.,b:Turn off all lights to conserve battery.,c:Use only parking lights without flashers.
note: When stopped at night, keep low-beam headlights on and use emergency flashers so other road users can clearly see your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway you should generally:
options: a:Use the on-ramp to accelerate to the speed of traffic and merge smoothly.,b:Proceed slowly on the ramp and merge at a lower speed.,c:Turn on your hazard lights while merging.
note: Use the acceleration lane to reach freeway speed so you can merge safely with existing traffic; entering traffic must yield.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Go to the next exit.,b:Make a U-turn across the median.,c:Stop and back up to the exit.
note: Do not stop, back up, or cross medians. Continue to the next exit and re-route back to your destination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you expect when approaching a heavy truck while driving uphill from behind?
options: a:The truck may be moving slower than the posted speed limit.,b:You may not be able to legally pass the truck.,c:You should always attempt to pass quickly.
note: Large vehicles often travel below the posted speed while climbing hills; exercise caution and do not pass on hills with limited visibility.

question: What should you do if an aggressive driver is behind you?
options: a:Make every effort to get out of the aggressive driver's way and avoid eye contact.,b:Stare at the driver as they pass to warn them.,c:Speed up to challenge them.,d:Brake suddenly to show displeasure.
note: When faced with an aggressive driver, safely move out of their way and avoid engagement or provocation.

question: Which action helps reduce the chance of a rear-end collision?
options: a:Check mirrors and blind spots before stopping.,b:Brake suddenly to alert following drivers.,c:Release the accelerator to let the vehicle slow, then apply steady pressure to the brake.,d:Flash your lights to warn drivers behind you.
note: To avoid rear-end collisions, release the accelerator to slow, then apply steady steady brake pressure so your stop is smooth and your brake lights warn drivers behind you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When meeting an oncoming vehicle on a narrow road, you must:
options: a:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the roadway.,b:Demand the other driver pull over entirely.,c:Pull completely off the road and stop regardless of road width.
note: On narrow roads both drivers should leave sufficient space; you must allow at least half the main-traveled portion for the oncoming vehicle to pass.

question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing where there is no traffic signal?
options: a:The driver must yield to the pedestrian.,b:The pedestrian must yield to the turning driver.,c:Whoever started moving last must yield.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at intersections without traffic signals, whether or not a marked crosswalk exists.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching a traffic signal that's been green for a long time, what should you do?
options: a:Prepare for it to change to yellow and begin slowing.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Assume it will remain green and continue at current speed.,d:Stop immediately before the light.
note: A long green may soon change; slow and prepare to stop when safe if it turns yellow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Signaling before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb is:
options: a:Required by law and a good driving habit.,b:Necessary only if other traffic is present.,c:Required only during the maneuver, not beforehand.,d:Optional on multilane roads.
note: The law requires that you signal for at least 100 feet before you move your vehicle to the right or left; signaling is also a good driving habit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal turns green, what is a required action before proceeding?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection.,b:Accelerate as quickly as possible.,c:Back up slowly if necessary.
note: A green light permits movement, but yield to any pedestrians or vehicles already in the intersection.

question: How should you reduce the effects of headlight glare from oncoming traffic at night?
options: a:Look toward the right side of the road ahead.,b:Look straight ahead.,c:Look over your shoulder.
note: To reduce blinding glare from oncoming headlights, focus on the right edge of the road or white line and avoid staring directly at the lights.

question: What should you check regarding your tires before driving?
options: a:The tread depth and that air pressure is adequate (no flat tires).,b:Only that they appear circular.,c:Only that they are not wet.
note: Ensure tires have sufficient tread and correct pressure; a flat or underinflated tire makes driving unsafe.

question: What do orange traffic signs typically indicate?
options: a:Work zone or construction area warnings.,b:Regulatory rules such as speed limits.,c:School zone areas.,d:Hospital zones.
note: Orange signs are used for highway work or construction warnings; they often are diamond-shaped with black symbols or text.

question: Why should you not follow other vehicles too closely?
options: a:You may not have enough time to stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.,b:You won't be able to see the rear lights.,c:You may not see the road between the cars.,d:It reduces your fuel efficiency.
note: Following too closely reduces the time and distance available to stop safely if the vehicle ahead brakes suddenly.

question: Which factor greatly affects your ability to stop quickly?
options: a:The condition of the road surface.,b:The color of your vehicle.,c:The number of passengers in your car.
note: Road conditions (wet, icy, gravel) strongly affect braking distance. Reduce speed when road conditions are poor to maintain control.

question: When sharing the road with trucks, remember they generally:
options: a:Require longer distances to stop and more space to maneuver than smaller vehicles.,b:Require less stopping distance than passenger cars.,c:Have smaller blind spots than cars.
note: Due to their size and weight, trucks need more room to stop and maneuver, and they have significant blind spots.

question: When you hear a siren behind you while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Pull over to the right and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.,b:Speed up to create space quickly.,c:Stop immediately in the middle of the lane.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching from behind, yield by safely pulling over to the right and stopping until it has passed; if heavy traffic prevents this, keep moving slowly until you can clear the way.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with no signals, you should:
options: a:Always come to a complete stop.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop if a train is coming.,c:Assume all crossings have signals and proceed normally.
note: At an unprotected railroad crossing, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should drivers do when approaching a flashing yellow traffic signal?
options: a:Increase their speed to clear the area.,b:Stop before proceeding.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light warns of a potential hazard — slow down and proceed carefully through the intersection.

question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:
options: a:Driving too fast for the wet road surface.,b:Making sudden stops.,c:Driving through shallow water.
note: Hydroplaning occurs when tires lose contact with the road surface due to water and excessive speed; slow down in wet conditions.

question: When passing a parked vehicle, what should you be prepared for?
options: a:A person or vehicle might unexpectedly move into your lane.,b:Pedestrians and drivers will always respect your right-of-way.,c:You should honk to alert them before passing.
note: Leave space when passing parked cars and be prepared for doors opening, people stepping out, or vehicles pulling away from the curb unexpectedly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive simultaneously at an open intersection, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:The driver signaling first has the right-of-way.,d:The larger vehicle has the right-of-way.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to the vehicle on your right if you arrive simultaneously.

question: How is defensive driving best defined?
options: a:Driving aggressively to gain position in traffic.,b:Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.,c:Driving against the flow of traffic if necessary.
note: Defensive driving means adjusting to road and traffic conditions, anticipating hazards, and taking steps to avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When driving so slowly that it disrupts the normal flow of traffic.,b:When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.,c:Only when driving in rural areas.
note: Driving so slowly that you disrupt traffic flow is illegal and can lead to a citation for impeding traffic.

question: What can happen to a bicyclist who disobeys traffic laws?
options: a:They can be ticketed just like motor vehicle drivers.,b:They are always given only a warning.,c:They are exempt from traffic laws.
note: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicle drivers; they can be cited for traffic violations.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, you should:
options: a:Slam on the brakes immediately.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and gradually slow to a stop.,c:Keep driving at the same speed until you reach your destination.
note: If a tire blows out, grip the wheel tightly, stay in your lane, ease off the accelerator, and gradually slow before braking and pulling off to safety.

question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Look over your shoulder toward the direction you intend to move.,b:Rely solely on your side mirrors.,c:Only check the rearview mirror.
note: Before changing lanes, glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check the blind spot in addition to using mirrors.

question: When preparing to change lanes, what minimum-sized gap should you look for?
options: a:Four- or five-second gap in the lane you want to enter.,b:One-second gap.,c:Two-second gap.,d:Only a half-second gap.
note: Identify a four- or five-second gap to change lanes safely, signal, check mirrors and blind spots, then merge.

question: A double solid yellow centerline on a two-lane road means:
options: a:Traffic flows in opposite directions and passing is prohibited for both directions.,b:Lanes go the same direction and passing is allowed.,c:You may pass if you are careful.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposite directions and mean no passing from either direction.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what actions should you take?
options: a:Slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop.,b:Speed up to cross before a train arrives.,c:Ignore signs if there are no gates.,d:Proceed unless you hear a horn.
note: When you see signs indicating a nearby railroad crossing, slow down, look for trains, and be prepared to stop. If red lights flash or gates are down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks.

question: Signs that warn of hazardous conditions ahead are classified as:
options: a:Warning signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Warning signs alert you to potential hazards so you can adjust speed or driving accordingly; obey them for safety.

question: Why is it important to leave a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.,b:It prevents all distractions from other vehicles.,c:It keeps traffic flowing evenly.
note: Maintaining ample space around your vehicle provides time and room to maneuver if another driver makes an error or a hazard appears.

question: What does a red arrow displayed on a traffic signal require of drivers?
options: a:Proceed slowly through the intersection.,b:Stop and then proceed when the way is clear.,c:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or a green arrow appears.
note: A red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow allows the movement.

question: When in a line of traffic crossing a railroad track with no signals or gates, what must you ensure?
options: a:Make sure there is enough space ahead so your vehicle can fully clear the tracks without stopping.,b:You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.,c:You may pass slower drivers while on the tracks.,d:Always stop halfway on the tracks to check for trains.
note: Ensure there is room on the far side of the tracks before proceeding so you won't be trapped on them if traffic stops.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do your vehicle's brake lights communicate to drivers behind you?
options: a:You are slowing down or stopping.,b:You are making a turn.,c:You have the emergency brake engaged.,d:You are changing lanes.
note: Brake lights indicate you are slowing or stopping and must be kept in working order so other drivers know your intentions.

question: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign warn you about?
options: a:Existing or possible road hazards.,b:Public recreation areas.,c:School zones.
note: Diamond-shaped signs warn of potential or existing hazards ahead and are usually yellow (or orange in temporary situations).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit or turn on a freeway, what is the correct action?
options: a:Continue to the next exit or safe location to turn around.,b:Stop and back up on the freeway shoulder.,c:Make an immediate turn from your current lane.
note: Do not back up or make sudden lane changes on the highway; proceed to the next exit or other safe location to turn around.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a multilane road when you see a 'Merging traffic' sign, how should you respond?
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles by changing lanes if safe.,b:Always maintain your present speed even if someone is trying to merge.,c:Honk at incoming traffic to warn them.
note: Allow merging vehicles room to enter. If it's safe and there is no one beside you, move over one lane to help traffic flow.

question: If you are in the right lane of a multilane highway and want to move left, what steps should you take?
options: a:Check mirrors, look over your left shoulder for blind spots, and signal before changing lanes.,b:Turn on your headlights and then move, without checking mirrors.,c:Only look into your rearview mirror before moving.
note: Always check rearview and side mirrors, glance over your shoulder into the blind spot, and signal before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What greatly increases stopping distance and crash severity?
options: a:High speeds.,b:Slow speeds.,c:Night driving.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distances and the energy involved in a collision, leading to more severe crashes.

question: Approximately how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph require to stop?
options: a:About 50 feet.,b:About 125 feet.,c:About 400 feet.,d:About 200 feet.
note: Large tractor-trailers require much longer stopping distances; at 55 mph a fully loaded rig can take nearly 400 feet to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when entering a public road from a private driveway or private road?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway before entering.,b:Blow your horn to warn approaching cars.,c:Pull partway onto the road and stop to alert drivers.
note: When entering from a driveway or private road, you must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and to vehicles on the public roadway.

question: If there's an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, how should you handle passing?
options: a:Let the oncoming car pass first, then safely pass the bicyclist so you only deal with one hazard at a time.,b:Try to split the difference and squeeze between both hazards.,c:Pull onto the shoulder to pass both at once.
note: When two hazards are present, handle them sequentially—allow the oncoming vehicle to pass first, then pass the bicyclist when safe.

question: When traffic signals are horizontal, where is the yellow light located?
options: a:In the middle.,b:On the left.,c:On the right.
note: On horizontal traffic signals the yellow light is in the middle; red is typically on the left and green on the right.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light indicate?
options: a:Proceed with caution.,b:A requirement to stop fully.,c:Pedestrian-only crossing.
note: A flashing yellow signal means slow down and proceed with caution; yield to pedestrians and traffic as needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill next to a curb, which way should you turn your steering wheel?
options: a:Turn the wheel away from the curb and set the parking brake.,b:Keep the front tires straight ahead.,c:Turn the wheel toward the curb and set the parking brake.,d:Leave the wheel straight and do not use parking brake.
note: When parked uphill with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb so a rolling vehicle will hit the curb instead of rolling into traffic.

question: How can drivers prevent drowsiness on long trips?
options: a:Stop regularly to rest and stretch.,b:Slow down and drive more cautiously.,c:Turn up the radio volume continuously.
note: Scheduling regular breaks to rest and stretch reduces drowsiness and helps drivers stay alert on long journeys.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the definition of a speed limit?
options: a:The maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions.,b:The suggested speed under dangerous conditions.,c:The required speed during rain.
note: A speed limit sets the legal maximum (or minimum where posted) under ideal conditions; adjust speed lower when conditions make the posted limit unsafe.

question: If you're angry after a work incident, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Take a few minutes to calm down before getting behind the wheel.,b:Drive fast on the highway to blow off steam.,c:Play loud music to mask your emotions while driving.
note: If upset or distracted, take time to cool off before driving; emotional driving impairs judgment and is dangerous.

question: Which safety restraint combination provides the most protection in a crash?
options: a:Only a lap belt.,b:Only an airbag.,c:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
note: Lap and shoulder belts combined with airbags provide the best protection in many frontal crashes when used properly.

question: In the SIPDE process, what does the I stand for?
options: a:Identify hazards.,b:Ignore distractions.,c:Increase speed.
note: The I in SIPDE stands for Identify — take notice of hazards, traffic signs, and potential problems ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a busy freeway, what is the proper way to merge into traffic?
options: a:Use the acceleration lane to match the freeway traffic speed and yield to vehicles already on the freeway.,b:Use only your mirrors and immediately merge at any speed.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a large gap.,d:Signal and enter without checking blind spots.
note: Use the entrance ramp to accelerate to freeway speed, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield to traffic already on the freeway before merging.

question: What should you remember about wet pavement and rainfall?
options: a:Pavement is especially slippery right after it starts to rain.,b:Wet roads never cause hydroplaning.,c:You do not need extra space when stopping on wet pavement.
note: Road surfaces can be especially slick immediately after rainfall due to oils and debris. Reduce speed and increase following distance when roads are wet to reduce risk of loss of traction.

question: Which medications can impair your driving ability?
options: a:Only diet pills.,b:Any medication.,c:Only prescription painkillers.,d:Only over-the-counter cold medicine.
note: Any medication may affect your ability to drive. Ask your doctor or pharmacist about side effects and read labels on prescriptions and over-the-counter drugs.

question: Your risk of being killed is how many times greater if you are thrown from a vehicle in a crash?
options: a:10 times.,b:25 times.,c:20 times.
note: Wearing a seat belt greatly reduces risk; being ejected from a vehicle makes your chance of fatal injury many times higher (about 25×).

question: When making a turn, what should you look at?
options: a:Look as far ahead around the bend as possible in the direction you want to go.,b:Watch only the cars behind you.,c:Look only at vegetation that blocks your view.,d:Focus solely on the curb.
note: When turning, look as far ahead as possible in the direction you intend to go to give yourself more time to react and make a smoother turn.

question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Early enough that other drivers understand your intention before you begin the maneuver.,b:Just before changing lanes.,c:After you start passing.,d:Only if the vehicle you are passing signals.
note: Signal in plenty of time before passing so other drivers know your intentions; do not signal only at the last moment.

question: Which is a good habit of a defensive driver?
options: a:Always driving slowly no matter the conditions.,b:Watching for the actions of other drivers and anticipating hazards.,c:Traveling at a constant speed regardless of conditions.
note: A defensive driver remains alert to the actions of others, anticipates problems, and adjusts driving accordingly.

question: What may happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of alcohol and the drug may both be increased.,b:Nothing will happen.,c:The effects of both will always be reduced.
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs can increase impairment and produce effects greater than either substance alone.

question: When stopped on an uphill slope, you should allow a larger space cushion:
options: a:In front of your vehicle.,b:At intersections only.,c:At a stop sign only.
note: Allow more space in front of your vehicle when stopped on an incline so a vehicle behind rolling back won't hit you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are in a lane marked for turning but you want to go straight, what should you do?
options: a:Reverse your vehicle and merge back into traffic.,b:Put on your signal and wait to merge into through-traffic.,c:Complete the turn as required by the lane.
note: If you are in a turn-only lane, other drivers expect you to turn. Do the turn and find another route to return to your intended direction.

question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the signal, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and allow the pedestrians to cross safely.,b:Honk to warn them and continue.,c:Speed up to pass in front of them.,d:Proceed as usual because you have the right-of-way.
note: Even with a green light you must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and allow them to cross safely.

question: What does a regulatory sign with a red circle and slash generally mean?
options: a:The indicated action is prohibited.,b:Drivers must come to a complete stop.,c:Some drivers must yield to others.
note: A red circle with a diagonal slash over a black symbol means the depicted action is forbidden under the regulation.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, what steps must you take?
options: a:Turn off the engine only.,b:Lock the ignition and remove the key.,c:Set the parking brake only.
note: When leaving a vehicle unattended, turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing yellow traffic signal at an intersection means you should:
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Continue through at the same speed you were traveling.
note: A flashing yellow light signals caution: slow down, look for hazards, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Slow down after you enter the exit ramp, not before.,b:Slow down before entering the ramp.,c:Keep your speed constant throughout the ramp.
note: Do not slow on the freeway travel lane; move onto the exit ramp and then reduce speed in the ramp's deceleration area.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, you should:
options: a:Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself.,b:Work hard to steer, reduce speed, and pull off to a safe location to stop.,c:Honk repeatedly and turn off the ignition immediately.
note: If power steering stops working, you will need more effort to steer. Reduce speed, carefully drive to a safe location, and stop.

question: What is the best way to deal with a driver who is tailgating you?
options: a:Slam on your brakes to teach them a lesson.,b:Speed up to increase the distance between you.,c:Change lanes or gradually slow down to encourage them to pass.,d:Brake-check them.
note: If another vehicle follows too closely, slow down and let it pass when it is safe; check traffic behind you regularly.

question: If stopped at a railroad crossing that has more than one track, you should:
options: a:Proceed as soon as one train passes.,b:Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks before proceeding.,c:Cross immediately because only one train can pass at a time.
note: At crossings with multiple tracks, wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before proceeding; another train may be approaching.

question: Which statement about passing motorcycles is correct?
options: a:You must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.,b:It is okay to follow motorcycles closely.,c:A motorcycle with two people is more stable than one with a single rider.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane; when passing a motorcycle, move completely into the adjacent lane—do not share the lane with the motorcycle.

question: If an emergency vehicle using lights or siren approaches you on a one-way street, you must:
options: a:Drive with your hazard lights on.,b:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,c:Speed up and leave the street as fast as possible.
note: On a one-way street, move toward the nearest roadside and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer is directing traffic at an intersection with functioning signals, whose directions must you follow?
options: a:The traffic light's indications.,b:The officer's directions.,c:Whichever is more convenient.
note: When an officer is directing traffic, follow their directions even if they conflict with traffic signals.

question: When borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Familiarize yourself with the controls (lights, wipers, brakes, horn, gear selector) and check for defects.,b:Assume everything works the same and drive immediately.,c:Hide from the owner that you are unsure of the vehicle.
note: Before driving a vehicle you are unfamiliar with, learn the location and operation of basic controls and correct any obvious defects first.

question: Which action best ensures safety when backing a vehicle?
options: a:Check behind the vehicle before you get in and back up.,b:Rely only on rearview mirrors while inside the vehicle.,c:Sound your horn just before shifting into reverse.
note: Before backing, get out and check behind the vehicle for children and obstacles; do not rely solely on mirrors or sensors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes on a highway, what steps should you take?
options: a:Signal your lane change, b:Check your rearview and outside mirrors, c:Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder, d:All of the above
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to ensure the blind spot is clear.

question: Why is night driving more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:Visibility is reduced in the dark, shrinking your field of vision.,b:Cars overheat more at night.,c:It is more likely to be raining at night.
note: The darkness limits what you can see; use headlights appropriately and drive at a safe speed for the conditions.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line only.,b:Passing permitted from either direction.,c:Passing permitted from the lane next to the solid line.,d:No passing permitted in either direction.
note: When a broken yellow line is beside a solid yellow line, traffic next to the broken line may pass when safe; the solid-line side may not pass.

question: When making a turn, what should you do with your speed?
options: a:Reduce your speed to maintain control.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Vary your speed unpredictably.
note: Slow to a safe speed before and during the turn so you can stay in your lane and respond to unexpected hazards.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the right (toward the curb).,b:Turn your wheels to the left (away from the curb).,c:Keep the wheels straight ahead.
note: When parked facing downhill, turn the wheels toward the curb so that if the vehicle rolls, it will move off the roadway rather than into traffic.

question: When is it appropriate to begin accelerating during a turn?
options: a:Begin accelerating near the middle of the curve after you have established your path.,b:Before you begin the turn.,c:Immediately after you start the turn.,d:Only after you reach the halfway point in the bend.
note: Begin to accelerate near the middle of the corner once your vehicle is aligned with the travel path and you can see through the turn.

question: If an oncoming car has blinding headlights, you should:
options: a:Look toward the right edge of the road until it passes.,b:Use your high beams so you can see better.,c:Flash your lights to warn the other driver.
note: When facing blinding headlights, avert your gaze to the right edge of the road until the vehicle passes to avoid temporary blindness.

question: What do solid white stop lines painted across lanes indicate?
options: a:Stop lines mark the exact location to stop at intersections and crosswalks.,b:They are painted only in curves and on hills.,c:They indicate church and school zones.,d:They mark no-parking areas.
note: Stop lines are solid white lines indicating where drivers must stop at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.

question: Which statement about driving in changing weather is true?
options: a:A sudden change in weather requires adjusting your driving (e.g., slow down in rain or fog).,b:You should always maintain the same speed regardless of weather.,c:Be less aware of vehicles behind you in bad weather.,d:Turn on cruise control in rain.
note: When weather changes, adjust driving accordingly by slowing down and increasing caution; be mindful of other vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended downward, what is that hand signal indicating?
options: a:The driver plans to turn left.,b:The driver plans to turn right.,c:The driver plans to stop or slow down.
note: A left arm extended downward signals that the driver intends to slow or stop. Adjust your driving accordingly if you see this signal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a stop sign, how should you scan before proceeding?
options: a:Look left first, then right, then left again before moving forward.,b:Only check behind you for tailgaters.,c:Move as soon as the vehicle ahead moves.
note: At a stop sign, check left because vehicles from that direction are closer, then right, and left again to ensure the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic signal requires drivers to:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and go only when safe.,c:Merge to the right immediately.
note: A flashing red light should be treated like a stop sign: stop, yield, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: An emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights approaches from behind. What must you do?
options: a:Continue driving and try to stay out of its way.,b:See if you can reach your destination before it catches up.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop when safe.
note: You must yield to emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights. Where possible, pull to the right edge of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it before pulling over.

question: If the solid white edge line on the right slants toward the left, what does that indicate?
options: a:The road will narrow ahead.,b:An intersection is just ahead.,c:A construction zone is ahead.
note: An edge line that angles toward the center means the roadway will narrow ahead; the edge of the travel lane is moving inward.

question: Which of the following actions can cause distracted driving?
options: a:Eating, talking/texting, or changing the radio.,b:Only talking on the phone.,c:Only looking at reading material occasionally.
note: Many activities—eating, drinking, smoking, interacting with devices, or adjusting controls—distract drivers and increase crash risk.

question: Which behavior may indicate a drunk driver?
options: a:Weaving between lanes.,b:Driving slightly slower than traffic.,c:Maintaining a constant speed.
note: Weaving, sudden swerving, erratic lane changes, and abrupt stops are common signs of impaired driving.

question: What effect does alcohol have on driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It helps driving skills but harms judgement.,b:It harms both driving skills and judgement.,c:It has no effect on either.
note: Alcohol impairs reaction time, vision, perception, and judgment, increasing the risk of crashes.

question: When should you use one-hand steering?
options: a:Only when backing or operating controls that require a brief reach.,b:For high-speed maneuvers to increase control.,c:When avoiding hazards at high speed.,d:At all times when driving in town.
note: Use one-hand steering only for backing or when briefly reaching to operate controls such as wipers or headlights.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.,b:When exiting an expressway.,c:When following a motorcycle.
note: Increase following distance in situations that reduce visibility or vehicle control—behind large trucks, in bad weather, heavy traffic, when following motorcycles/bicycles, or when someone is tailgating you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you always use a turn signal?
options: a:When changing lanes.,b:When pulling into or out of a parking space.,c:When pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
note: Always signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of parking, or entering traffic from an alley or parking area to communicate your intentions.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Drive more slowly.,b:Drive more quickly.,c:Drive through standing water deliberately.
note: Because hydroplaning risk increases with speed on wet roads, reducing speed lowers the chance your tires will ride on water.

question: What do downward-pointing triangular signs usually indicate?
options: a:Yield — slow and give right-of-way when necessary.,b:School zones.,c:Construction ahead.,d:No U-turn.
note: A downward-pointing triangle typically indicates a yield sign: slow and give right-of-way as required.

question: If an intersection's traffic signals are out because of a power outage, you should treat it as:
options: a:A four-way stop—stop and proceed when it's your turn.,b:A place to turn on hazard lights and go through without stopping.,c:A location to park and wait for power to be restored.
note: When signals are not functioning, approach as you would a four-way stop: stop, then proceed in turn when safe.

question: What is a vehicle's blind spot?
options: a:An area you cannot see without turning your head.,b:The area directly behind your vehicle only.,c:The view you have in your rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are zones around the vehicle not visible in mirrors; you must turn your head to check them before lane changes.

question: What does a solid red arrow in a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Traffic in the indicated lane must stop and may not turn in that direction.,b:It means the same as a green light.,c:It is only advisory and may be ignored if clear.,d:Drivers may turn after yielding to oncoming traffic.
note: A solid red arrow has the same force as a circular red light — you must stop and may not turn in the arrow's direction.

question: What is a good practice to relieve fatigue on a long trip?
options: a:Stop and rest approximately every two hours.,b:Drive continuously and keep caffeine levels high.,c:Do arm exercises while driving.,d:Drive with one eye open at a time to stay alert.
note: To avoid fatigue, stop regularly (about every two hours) for short breaks or rest before resuming driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a single broken yellow centerline indicate on a two-lane road?
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is permitted when safe.,b:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is prohibited.,c:Traffic must stay in the right lane at all times.
note: A single broken yellow line separates opposite-direction traffic and indicates passing is allowed when it is safe to do so.

question: When you hear or see an emergency vehicle approaching, what should you do on a two-lane or undivided highway?
options: a:Stop immediately in the lane where you are driving.,b:Drive as far to the right as is safe and stop.,c:Slow down and keep moving at a reduced speed.
note: On two-lane roads, pull as far right as safely possible and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.

question: What is the vertical order of traffic lights from top to bottom?
options: a:Red on top, yellow in the middle, green on the bottom.,b:Red on top, green in the middle, yellow on the bottom.,c:Green on top, red in the middle, yellow on the bottom.,d:Green on top, yellow in the middle, red on the bottom.
note: On vertically arranged signals, red is always at the top, yellow in the middle, and green at the bottom.

question: If another vehicle seems likely to hit you, what is the appropriate action to warn them?
options: a:Wave your arms.,b:Use your emergency lights.,c:Sound your horn.
note: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians when you believe they may not see you and a collision might occur.

question: Is it legal to drink alcoholic beverages in a vehicle on a public highway?
options: a:Yes, if you are not the driver.,b:Yes, if you are riding in the back seat.,c:No, it is illegal to possess or consume an open alcoholic beverage on a public road.
note: It is illegal to consume or possess open alcoholic beverages on public roads; open container laws prohibit storing an open container where driver or passenger sits.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim high beams, which part of the road should you look toward?
options: a:The right side of the road.,b:The center of the road.,c:Either side.,d:The oncoming vehicle's headlights.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded by oncoming high beams while maintaining your lane position.

question: Which technique helps avoid crashes when driving on snowy or icy roads?
options: a:Reduce speed and increase following distance.,b:Get off highways as quickly as possible.,c:Add extra weight to improve traction.,d:Use cruise control to maintain speed.
note: On snow or ice, reduce your speed and increase your following distance; avoid sudden maneuvers and do not use cruise control.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by what color line?
options: a:White lines.,b:Yellow lines.,c:Red lines.
note: White lines separate lanes traveling in the same direction. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must traffic signs and pavement markings be treated by drivers?
options: a:They must always be obeyed.,b:They are optional suggestions.,c:Only obey them when other vehicles are present.,d:Follow them only at night.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and must be obeyed at all times.

question: What is a likely effect of eating or drinking while driving?
options: a:It distracts you and makes staying in your lane and controlling the vehicle more difficult.,b:It makes you a better driver because you are less hungry.,c:It causes no driving errors.
note: Eating and drinking divert hands and attention from driving, increasing the likelihood of lane wander and other control errors.

question: How do blind spots compare on larger vehicles versus smaller?
options: a:Larger vehicles have larger blind spots.,b:Larger vehicles have smaller blind spots.,c:Larger vehicles have no blind spots.,d:Blind spots are the same regardless of vehicle size.
note: Bigger vehicles (trucks, buses) have larger blind spots, especially near the rear and sides, compared to passenger cars.

question: If a pedestrian begins crossing in front of your vehicle, you should:
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop; yield the right-of-way.,b:Flash your lights to warn them.,c:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.,d:Honk continuously to hurry them.
note: Slow down and be prepared to stop whenever pedestrians are walking on or crossing the roadway. Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in crosswalks.

question: You are approaching a railroad crossing and you do not see or hear a train. Under which conditions must you still stop?
options: a:Only if lights are flashing.,b:If a stop sign is posted, if crossing lights are flashing, or if a gate is lowered.,c:Only if a crossing gate is lowered.
note: You must always stop if a stop sign is posted, crossing gates are lowered, lights are flashing, a flagger signals you, or a train is visible and close enough to be hazardous.

question: Many crashes are caused by which of the following?
options: a:Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.,b:Drivers consistently checking mirrors and blind spots.,c:Drivers yielding the right-of-way.
note: Driving too fast for road or weather conditions is a common contributing factor in crashes; adjust speed to conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light as you approach, what should you do?
options: a:Accelerate to avoid a red light.,b:Continue as you have the right-of-way.,c:Slow and prepare to stop unless you are already in the intersection.
note: A steady yellow means the light is about to turn red; slow and stop if it is safe to do so unless you are already in the intersection.

question: A steady green traffic light at an intersection means you may:
options: a:Proceed through the intersection if the way is clear and yield to pedestrians and other vehicles as required.,b:Always speed up to get through before the light changes.,c:Stop and wait for a green arrow before moving.
note: A steady green allows you to go if it is safe; you may also turn (yielding to pedestrians and oncoming traffic) unless signs prohibit it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are in the left lane and want to move right, what checks should you make before changing lanes?
options: a:Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for vehicles in the right lane.,b:Check mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder only.,c:Signal and change lanes without looking if clear in the mirror.,d:Check your mirrors then immediately change lanes.
note: When moving right from the left lane, check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder to clear the blind spot.

question: When turning left, on which traffic signal do you have the right-of-way?
options: a:A green arrow pointing left.,b:A solid green circular light.,c:A flashing yellow light.,d:A solid red light.
note: A steady green arrow authorizes protected left turns; oncoming traffic is required to stop for the turning traffic.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Use tires with proper air pressure and good tread.,b:Speed up to pass standing water quickly.,c:Turn on cruise control in wet conditions.,d:Drive with your parking lights on.
note: Hydroplaning risk is reduced by maintaining proper tire pressure and tread and by slowing on wet roads.

question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Pull alongside and yell at the driver.,b:Let it go and continue driving safely.,c:Flash your high beams to warn them.,d:Follow and confront them at the next stop.
note: To avoid road rage and danger, do not react aggressively. Let it go and continue driving safely.

question: On a two-lane road without bike lanes, how should you pass a bicyclist traveling in your direction?
options: a:Pass with at least three feet of clearance after ensuring no oncoming traffic.,b:Sound your horn and pass closely.,c:Wait until a traffic signal or stop sign before passing.,d:Speed up and pass quickly in the same lane.
note: Pass a bicyclist as you would another vehicle, leaving sufficient space (about 3 feet or more) and only when it is safe and clear of oncoming traffic.

question: Under normal driving conditions, what minimum following distance should you maintain?
options: a:One second.,b:Two seconds.,c:Three seconds.
note: Maintain at least a three-second following distance under normal conditions; increase it when weather or traffic makes driving less safe.

question: Which of the following is an effect of alcohol on driving ability?
options: a:Loss of concentration, poor coordination, and slower judgment.,b:Increased alertness and faster reflexes.,c:Improved night vision.,d:No effect if you feel sober.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair vision, judgment, coordination, and concentration.

question: What is the single most effective thing you can do to lower your risk of injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Wear your seat belt.,b:Limit driving to weekdays.,c:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.,d:Drive only during daylight.
note: Wearing your seat belt is the single most effective action to reduce the chance of death or serious injury in a crash.

question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass?
options: a:No, except to turn into or from a driveway or private road.,b:Yes, whenever there is no oncoming traffic.,c:Yes, if you are late for an appointment.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing for either direction, except when making a left turn into or out of a driveway, alley, or private road where permitted.

question: Which takes precedence over signs, signals, and pavement markings?
options: a:Directions from a police officer or authorized traffic control person.,b:A steady red light.,c:A stop sign.
note: Instructions from authorized traffic officers (police, flaggers, school crossing persons) override traffic signals and signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers may not pass from either direction where the centerline is:
options: a:Double solid yellow.,b:Single broken yellow.,c:Combination solid and broken yellow.
note: A double solid yellow centerline on a two-way road means passing is prohibited for traffic in both directions.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:
options: a:Overcorrect and steer sharply.,b:Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid.,c:Turn the wheel away from the direction of the skid.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, remain calm and steer in the direction of the skid to regain control.

question: What practice helps you avoid emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Look ahead and maintain a safe following distance.,b:Honk frequently to make others aware of you.,c:Stay only in the right lane regardless of speed.
note: Keeping a safe following distance and scanning ahead allows you to anticipate hazards and reduces the need for sudden stops that could cause rear-end collisions.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal warns that which light is about to appear?
options: a:Steady red.,b:Flashing yellow.,c:Steady green.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to change to a steady red; prepare to stop unless you are already in the intersection.

question: An octagonal traffic sign always means:
options: a:Speed limit.,b:Stop.,c:Hospital.
note: An eight-sided (octagonal) sign is always a stop sign. Come to a complete stop at the sign.

question: When should drivers use hand-over-hand steering?
options: a:When turning at low speeds such as at intersections or parking.,b:For high-speed evasive maneuvers.,c:Only when driving straight.
note: Hand-over-hand steering is appropriate for low-speed turns and maneuvering in tight spaces; other methods are better at higher speeds.

question: In the SIPDE process, what does the 'E' stand for?
options: a:Execute a maneuver (brake, accelerate, turn) to avoid a hazard.,b:Exhaust the brakes.,c:Elaborate on decisions.
note: The 'E' in SIPDE is 'Execute'—carry out a planned action such as braking, accelerating, or steering to respond to a hazard.

question: When is it appropriate to honk your horn?
options: a:When traveling through an intersection.,b:When passing a bicyclist.,c:When you see a child about to run into the street.
note: Use your horn as a warning when another road user does not see you and immediate attention is needed, such as a child stepping into the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning right on a green light, you must:
options: a:Maintain your normal driving speed.,b:Yield to pedestrians and other traffic in the intersection.,c:Stop and check for nearby police vehicles before turning.
note: On a green light you may turn unless prohibited, but you must yield to pedestrians and any vehicles already in the intersection.

question: When you approach an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights, you must:
options: a:Slow down and, if possible, change lanes to give the vehicle space.,b:Stop immediately in your lane.,c:Drive past without changing speed.
note: If an emergency, tow, or roadside assistance vehicle is stopped with flashing lights, change lanes away if safe; otherwise slow below the posted limit and proceed with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the best action when a traffic light turns from green to yellow as you approach an intersection?
options: a:Be prepared to stop if it is safe to do so.,b:Speed up to try to beat the red light.,c:Brake sharply to stop immediately.
note: A steady yellow light signals that it will soon change to red. Slow and be prepared to stop, if it can be done safely.

question: Why must you be cautious when passing a bicyclist?
options: a:You travel faster than the bicycle.,b:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass the bicyclist.
note: When passing a bicyclist, be cautious because the cyclist may swerve and oncoming traffic may not expect you to move into their lane.

question: Who must use a safety belt in Louisiana?
options: a:All occupants of the vehicle (driver and passengers).,b:Only the driver.,c:Only passengers in the front seat.,d:Only passengers under 18.
note: Louisiana law requires all motor vehicle occupants to be properly buckled in safety belts.

question: A red flashing traffic light is equivalent to which traffic control?
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A yield sign.,c:A steady red light.
note: A flashing red traffic signal has the same meaning as a stop sign: come to a complete stop, yield, and proceed when safe.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck (no gates or flashing lights), what should you do?
options: a:Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.,b:Turn your radio down and cross quickly.,c:Enter the crossing and trust other drivers to warn you.,d:Speed up to beat any possible train.
note: At crossings without active warnings, you must look and listen carefully and only cross when you know no train is approaching from either direction.

question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Do not proceed until the children wave to you.,b:Accelerate once the bus door closes.,c:Watch for children walking along the side of the road and proceed with caution.
note: When a bus has its stop arm extended and lights flashing, watch carefully for children near the roadway and proceed only when it is safe.

question: Red pavement markings or reflectors indicate what?
options: a:A roadway or lane that must not be entered (no entry).,b:Increased speed limits ahead.,c:A temporary slowdown area.,d:A designated passing zone.
note: Red pavement markings or reflectors mark areas that should not be entered; seeing them means you must turn around or not enter.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is a good practice when driving to an area you are not familiar with?
options: a:Rely only on road signs to find your way.,b:Plan your route in advance.,c:Drive with only a general idea of your destination.
note: Plan your trip before you leave. Familiarize yourself with the route so you can focus on driving safely.

question: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident, what should you do?
options: a:Move the vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway if possible.,b:Never move the vehicle under any circumstances.,c:Wait for police before moving it.
note: After a minor collision, move your vehicle off the road if it can be done safely; however, do not leave the scene without providing identification and assistance if needed.

question: When driving in rain, which headlights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: In rainy conditions, use low beam headlights to improve visibility and avoid glaring other drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you begin to slow down for a highway exit?
options: a:After you have moved into the exit lane.,b:Before you reach the exit lane on the main highway.,c:Only once you see the toll booth.
note: Move into the exit lane well before slowing; generally you should not decelerate on the main highway until after you have entered the exit lane.

question: Which springtime driving hazard is mentioned?
options: a:Increased potholes.,b:Improved traction everywhere.,c:Longer daylight hours only.
note: Spring can bring potholes from winter damage; additionally, allergy medications used in spring can impair driving, and rain can make roads slick.

question: A curb painted which color indicates handicap parking restriction?
options: a:Blue.,b:Yellow.,c:White.
note: Blue painted curbs indicate parking reserved for persons with disabilities.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:It is illegal to drive around lowered crossing gates, and not all crossings have flashing signals.,b:All crossings have flashing red signals and gates.,c:You may always drive around lowered gates if no train appears.
note: Not all railroad crossings have gates or lights; however, it is illegal to go around lowered gates. Obey flaggers and warning devices.

question: Under what condition may you cross a dashed white line?
options: a:At any time of day.,b:Only during daylight hours.,c:When it is safe to change lanes or pass.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and can be crossed to change lanes when safe.

question: If one of your tires blows out while driving, you should:
options: a:Brake hard immediately.,b:Try to steer straight and gradually slow by easing off the gas.,c:Maintain speed and steer as usual.
note: Hold the wheel firmly, keep the vehicle straight, ease off the gas, and do not apply the brakes until you have control; then pull off safely.

question: Which trait is characteristic of a defensive driver?
options: a:Anger.,b:Good judgment.,c:Passivity.
note: Defensive drivers use good judgment, anticipate hazards, and avoid risky maneuvers to remain safe.

question: Which is a safe technique for driving through a curve?
options: a:Slow down as you enter the curve and increase speed gradually as you exit.,b:Maintain exactly the same speed through the entire curve.,c:Speed up before entering the curve and slow down when exiting.
note: Slow before entering a curve and then gradually accelerate as you leave it to maintain control.

question: If a fire engine is following you on a two-lane street but is not using lights or siren, you should:
options: a:Continue to drive normally.,b:Stop immediately.,c:Speed up to get out of its way.
note: If an emergency vehicle is not using its siren or lights, you are not required to clear a path; continue driving normally.

question: Why should you adjust your headrest before driving?
options: a:Headrests help prevent whiplash in a collision.,b:They increase your seating comfort.,c:They improve rear visibility.
note: Headrests protect vehicle occupants from whiplash injuries; proper adjustment is an important safety step before driving.

question: If you drink alcohol socially, what helps ensure you get home safely?
options: a:Drink coffee before driving.,b:Take a cold shower before driving.,c:Arrange a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,d:Exercise to sober up.
note: To avoid impaired driving, arrange a sober ride home. Coffee, cold showers, and exercise do not lower blood alcohol concentration.

question: What should you do first when it starts to rain while you are driving?
options: a:Slow down and, if heavy rain reduces visibility, pull off and stop until it eases.,b:Drive faster than surrounding traffic to get through quickly.,c:Keep driving at the posted maximum speed regardless of conditions.
note: Reduce speed in rain, turn on headlights so others can see you, and if visibility becomes poor, safely pull onto the shoulder and stop until conditions improve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection or roadway.,b:Always come to a complete stop before proceeding.,c:Yield only to traffic on your left.,d:Ignore it if no cars are visible.
note: A yield sign requires you to slow and yield to others; stop only if necessary to avoid interfering with traffic.

question: When does stopping distance increase?
options: a:On a wet or icy road.,b:On paved highways.,c:Only when driving at night.
note: Stopping distances are longer on wet, icy, or loose surfaces and when road conditions are less than ideal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what circumstances may you cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:Never under any circumstance.,b:To turn left into a driveway or to make a permitted left turn.,c:To pass a slow-moving vehicle.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit lane changes for passing, but you may cross them to make a left turn into or out of a driveway or to perform a permitted left turn.

question: How can drivers avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Never pass them.,b:Avoid driving alongside them and do not tailgate.,c:Flash your lights to get their attention.
note: Large vehicles have significant blind spots; avoid lingering beside them and do not tailgate to stay visible to the driver.

question: When parking uphill with a curb, you should:
options: a:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,b:Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb so if the vehicle rolls it will move away from traffic.

question: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, what is the correct way to return to the pavement?
options: a:Slow down and carefully steer back onto the pavement.,b:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.,c:Stop on the edge of the road.
note: Reduce speed without heavy braking and steer carefully back onto the roadway when safe to do so, checking for traffic before re-entering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should you avoid when preparing to change lanes?
options: a:Failing to check your side and rearview mirrors.,b:Using your turn signal to indicate your intention.,c:Checking for other drivers who may be moving into the same lane.
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors, signal, and check for drivers who might also be attempting to enter that lane.

question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Exit the roadway and take a short nap.,b:Drink more coffee and keep driving.,c:Turn up the radio loudly to stay awake.
note: If rest doesn't help, safely exit the highway and take a short nap—drowsy driving is dangerous.

question: Which is a trait of a defensive driver?
options: a:Being alert and anticipating potential dangers.,b:Reacting with anger and aggression.,c:Being passive and ignoring hazards.
note: A defensive driver predicts hazards, stays alert, and prepares to act to avoid danger rather than reacting emotionally.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,b:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.,c:Drivers should make hand motions to decide who goes first.
note: At simultaneous arrivals to a four-way stop, the vehicle on the left must yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on the right; otherwise, vehicles proceed in arrival order.

question: How should you safely pass a bicyclist?
options: a:Drive in the bicycle lane until you can safely pass.,b:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much room as possible.,c:Honk to warn the bicyclist to move over.
note: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and give them as much lateral space as possible; do not crowd or startle them.

question: How far ahead should you typically look while driving to avoid last-second braking or sudden turns?
options: a:About 10 to 15 seconds ahead.,b:One to three seconds ahead.,c:Five to seven seconds ahead.
note: To avoid last-minute maneuvers, scan at least 10–15 seconds ahead of your vehicle; this gives you time to react and allows drivers behind you to anticipate your actions.

question: On a road without sidewalks, which way should a pedestrian walk?
options: a:On the side facing oncoming traffic.,b:On the side where traffic is moving in the same direction.,c:On the side with the lightest traffic.
note: When there are no sidewalks, pedestrians should walk facing oncoming traffic so they can see vehicles and react as needed.

question: What is 'highway hypnosis' and how does it occur?
options: a:A condition caused by staring at the roadway for long periods which reduces active scanning.,b:Improved focus from frequent rest stops.,c:Too much sleep the night before a trip.,d:Increased alertness after driving nonstop.
note: 'Highway hypnosis' results when drivers stare ahead for long periods and stop actively scanning, which can lead to zoning out and crashes.

question: When should drivers use hand-to-hand (push/pull) steering?
options: a:During normal driving at speeds above about 15 mph.,b:When avoiding a hazard at high speed.,c:Only when parking at low speed.
note: Hand-to-hand steering (push/pull) is recommended for normal driving at higher speeds for smooth control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, you must:
options: a:Use the lane belonging to oncoming traffic only if it is safe and legal to do so.,b:Flash your lights to signal oncoming drivers.,c:Use the shoulder to pass when available.
note: Passing on a two-lane, two-way road may require entering the oncoming lane; only do so if you can complete the pass safely and legally.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs legally indicate?
options: a:Suggested speeds for comfortable driving.,b:The maximum or minimum speed that is legally allowed.,c:The speed drivers should use in heavy traffic.,d:The recommended speed for trucks only.
note: Speed limit signs indicate the maximum or minimum speed legally allowed under ideal conditions; you must slow down when conditions require it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive simultaneously, which is true?
options: a:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,b:The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.,c:The car on the left has the right-of-way.
note: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A flashing yellow light warns drivers to slow down and proceed with caution through the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-way, two-lane street, when is passing safe?
options: a:Only when you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic and can clearly see ahead.,b:Whenever the vehicle ahead is slower regardless of sight distance.,c:When you are able to clearly see the road ahead only.,d:If your vehicle is faster than the one ahead.
note: You may pass only if you can see clearly ahead, can return before meeting oncoming traffic, and it is legal and safe to do so.

question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Plan ahead and allow plenty of time so you do not need to speed or break rules.,b:Speed only when there are no police officers around.,c:Tailgate other drivers to signal urgency.
note: To reduce aggressive driving, give yourself enough time for trips, avoid confrontations, and do not respond to aggressive behavior with aggression.

question: What is the 'No zone' in relation to large trucks or buses?
options: a:The blind spots around a truck or bus where other vehicles cannot be seen.,b:A designated school zone near buses.,c:A special speed zone for large vehicles.,d:A prohibited parking zone.
note: The 'No zone' refers to the large blind spots around trucks and buses where smaller vehicles may disappear from the driver's view.

question: What does a single dashed yellow center line mean?
options: a:Traffic in both directions may pass when safe.,b:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,c:Drivers may not pass.
note: A single dashed yellow line separates opposing traffic and indicates that vehicles in either direction may pass when it is safe to do so.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:It can reduce your ability to concentrate and focus on driving.,b:It will decrease your accident risk.,c:It will make you fall asleep at the wheel.
note: Strong emotions or stress reduce concentration and impair driving ability; if upset, wait to drive until calm.

question: Which describes a trait of a good defensive driver?
options: a:Laziness.,b:Skill and awareness to avoid hazards.,c:Passivity.
note: A defensive driver has the skills to anticipate hazards, avoid distractions, and maintain safe road behavior.

question: A driver ahead is distracted, driving with one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?
options: a:Give the vehicle extra space by increasing your following distance.,b:Assume the driver will correct their behavior and follow closely.,c:Imitate the behavior to fit in with traffic flow.
note: If a nearby driver appears distracted, allow extra space because their risk of making an error is greater.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a roundabout you must slow down and yield to which of the following?
options: a:Vehicles already circulating in the roundabout.,b:Bicyclists and pedestrians in the roundabout.,c:All of the above: vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians.,d:Only to larger vehicles.
note: When entering a roundabout, yield to vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians already in or crossing into the roundabout.

question: What color are guide (directional) signs?
options: a:Green.,b:Yellow.,c:Red.
note: Guide signs that provide directional and mileage information generally have a green background with white letters and symbols.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:When the other vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.,b:Even if it means driving off the pavement.,c:On a narrow bridge.
note: You may pass on the right if the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is room to pass safely, or on multi-lane roads with lanes moving in the same direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should a driver who travels much slower than the speed limit do if traffic is backing up behind them on a two-lane road?
options: a:Pull off the roadway when safe to let other vehicles pass.,b:Maintain current speed because they have the right-of-way.,c:Refuse to let others pass.
note: If you're driving significantly below the normal flow and causing a queue, you must pull off the road when safe to allow others to pass.

question: How should you check your vehicle's blind spots?
options: a:Turn your head and look over your shoulder.,b:By checking your side mirrors only.,c:By looking in your rearview mirror.
note: To verify blind spots before lane changes, physically look over your shoulder in the direction of the move; mirrors alone are insufficient.

question: When is evasive-action steering used?
options: a:To avoid hazards at higher speeds where limited steering input is needed.,b:For normal low-speed turns.,c:Only while parked.
note: Evasive steering is used to avoid hazards at higher speeds; it requires limited input to prevent overcorrection and loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left, what should you do?
options: a:Signal several seconds in advance, move into the left lane on multilane roads, and watch for oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Speed up and turn quickly to beat oncoming traffic.,c:Ignore the rearview mirror and rely only on the turn signal.
note: Signal early, position your vehicle appropriately, check mirrors, and yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians before turning.

question: What can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Allowing extra travel time.,b:Obeying posted speed limits.,c:Using proper turn signals.,d:All of the above
note: Allow extra travel time, obey speed limits, and use signals to reduce stress and the likelihood of aggressive encounters.

question: When following an emergency vehicle, what minimum following distance should you keep?
options: a:Two seconds.,b:Four seconds.,c:Ten seconds.
note: Increase your following distance to at least four seconds when following an emergency vehicle so it has room to operate.

question: If someone is injured in an accident, you should:
options: a:Move the injured person immediately away from the scene.,b:Not move the injured unnecessarily and keep them warm while providing first aid.,c:Always leave the injured where they are and do nothing.
note: Do not move injured people unless necessary; keep them warm, provide first aid if trained, and wait for medical professionals to arrive.

question: If your vehicle has ABS and begins to lose traction, what is the correct braking technique?
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly and steer.,b:Pump the brakes manually.,c:Press and hold the gas pedal.
note: With Anti-Lock Braking System, apply firm, continuous pressure on the brake pedal and steer to safety; pumping the brakes or releasing pressure can disengage the ABS.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do before proceeding?
options: a:Drive slowly to let approaching vehicles get out of the way.,b:Honk to alert others.,c:Stop and proceed only when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
note: Always stop before entering the roadway from a driveway, yield to pedestrians and traffic, and make your stop before crossing the sidewalk area.

question: In the SIPDE process, what does the S represent?
options: a:Sweep, Search and Scan.,b:Stare ahead.,c:Slow down.
note: The S stands for Sweep, Search, and Scan — continually move your eyes to gather complete information about the roadway."

question: If your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement, what is the correct response?
