options: a:Take your foot off the accelerator, steer parallel to the road, slow down, and then ease back onto the pavement when safe.,b:Brake hard and stop immediately.,c:Turn sharply back onto the road at full speed.,d:Accelerate and quickly jerk the wheel back on the pavement.
note: If your right wheels exit the pavement, slow and steer steadily, then ease back onto the road when it is safe to do so.

question: When must you stop for a school bus that is loading or unloading children?
options: a:Only if you are on the same side and the bus is on the shoulder.,b:If you are on a two-lane highway and the bus's red lights are flashing.,c:Only if the bus displays no passengers.
note: On a two-lane highway, vehicles in both directions must stop when a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing and/or the stop arm extended.

question: From which areas of your vehicle should snow and ice be removed before driving?
options: a:Just the windshield.,b:All windows, the hood, and the roof.,c:Only the windshield and passenger window.
note: Remove all snow and ice from windows, hood, roof, and mirrors so you have clear visibility and to prevent ice or snow from falling onto other vehicles.

question: What color pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow.,b:White.,c:Yellow and white.
note: Yellow centerlines separate opposing traffic; white lines separate traffic moving in the same direction.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Drive faster than a train.,b:Stop if a train is nearby, and be prepared to yield.,c:Look for a way around any lowered gates.
note: Railroad warning signs mean a train could be approaching. Obey signals and do not go around lowered gates or active warnings.

question: What will help a person overcome the effects of alcohol?
options: a:Tomato juice and lime.,b:Hot coffee.,c:Only the passage of time.
note: Only time will reduce blood alcohol concentration. Myths like coffee, food, or fresh air do not speed up recovery.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a stop is required but no stop line or crosswalk is marked, where should you stop?
options: a:At the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic without entering it.,b:You are not required to stop in that case.,c:Only slow down and proceed if clear.,d:Stop at the center of the intersection.
note: Stop at the first point nearest the intersecting roadway that gives you a view of approaching traffic without entering the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you have the legal right-of-way at an intersection, how should you proceed?
options: a:Proceed cautiously; do not assume other drivers will obey right-of-way rules.,b:Speed up to get through the intersection quickly.,c:Wave other drivers forward to indicate your intent.
note: Even with the right-of-way, always verify other drivers' actions and proceed cautiously—do not assume others will obey rules.

question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is correct?
options: a:They have the right-of-way when using sirens and/or flashing lights.,b:You do not need to yield if they are on the other side of the street.,c:They never use loudspeakers.,d:You should always follow closely behind them.
note: Yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights and obey any instructions from their loudspeakers.

question: What does the slow-moving vehicle emblem indicate?
options: a:The vehicle is likely traveling 25 mph or slower (reflective orange triangle).,b:The vehicle will travel faster than the speed limit.,c:The vehicle is a commercial truck.
note: A reflective orange triangle marks a vehicle traveling at 25 mph or less; watch for slow speeds and pass only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you pass another vehicle on a two-lane road?
options: a:Only when there is no oncoming traffic and the passing maneuver is not prohibited by pavement markings.,b:In a curve or on a hill if it looks clear.,c:By driving onto the shoulder of the highway.
note: Do not pass on hills or curves where visibility is limited and never pass by driving onto the shoulder; only pass where markings and sight distance allow.

question: Which winter driving statement is NOT true?
options: a:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.,b:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,c:Check antifreeze and washer fluid levels before winter travel.
note: Do not use cruise control in snow, rain, or icy conditions. Winter driving is hazardous and requires extra precautions and equipment checks.

question: When driving near a motorcycle, what should you allow?
options: a:The motorcycle a full lane width.,b:To be passed in the same lane with you.,c:To use only half a lane.,d:To ride on the shoulder next to you.
note: Motorcycles are full-size vehicles legally entitled to a full lane; do not attempt to share a lane with them.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, how should you respond?
options: a:Flash your lights and argue with them.,b:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.,c:Attempt to block or retaliate.
note: Do not engage or escalate. Stay calm, get out of their way, and, if necessary, report aggressive drivers to authorities.

question: At a light rail intersection, what should you always do?
options: a:Obey signals and look both ways before crossing tracks.,b:Assume trains will yield to your vehicle.,c:Drive around lowered gates if no train is visible.
note: Always obey traffic controls at rail intersections, look both ways before crossing, and never go around lowered gates.

question: Where should you maintain a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:Only in front of your vehicle.,b:On all sides of your vehicle.,c:Only behind your vehicle.
note: Maintain a cushion of space on all sides of your vehicle to give yourself room to react to hazards and avoid collisions.

question: What does a red-and-white triangular sign at an intersection mean?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way; be prepared to stop if necessary.,b:Always come to a full stop.,c:Slow only if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
note: A red-and-white triangle indicates a yield sign: slow and yield to other vehicles or pedestrians, stopping if required by conditions.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, what assumption should you make?
options: a:Assume the driver may open a door into the roadway.,b:Speed up to get past quickly.,c:Slam on your brakes as you pass.
note: When passing parked cars, assume someone may open a door or step into the street. Use caution and give extra space.

question: A steady yellow arrow displayed at an intersection tells drivers to:
options: a:Stop if it is safe to do so because a red arrow is coming.,b:Merge into the direction indicated by the arrow.,c:Proceed with caution and turn without yielding.,d:Ignore the arrow and follow the circular light.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that the signal is about to change to red; you should stop if you can do so safely.

question: At night, which of the following is the hardest to see while driving?
options: a:Road signs.,b:Pedestrians.,c:Other motorists.
note: Pedestrians are the most difficult to see at night compared to road signs and other vehicles, making extra caution necessary.

question: Which is not a factor in stopping distance?
options: a:Steering ability.,b:Braking distance.,c:Reaction distance.,d:Perception time.
note: Stopping distance is based on perception, reaction, and braking distances — steering ability is not a direct factor.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady yellow traffic light at an intersection warns you to:
options: a:Go if the intersection is clear.,b:Slow down and prepare to stop.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming; slow down and prepare to stop unless you are already so close that stopping would be unsafe.

question: How should you drive on slippery roads?
options: a:Reduce speed and avoid sudden changes; do not use cruise control.,b:Always drive at the maximum speed limit.,c:Use cruise control to maintain steady speed.,d:Drive with emergency flashers on.
note: On slippery surfaces reduce speed, avoid sudden maneuvers, and do not use cruise control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must stop at an intersection when you see which signal?
options: a:A flashing red light.,b:A steady yellow light.,c:A yellow arrow.,d:A flashing green light.
note: A flashing red signal means the same as a stop sign: stop, look both ways, and proceed only when clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, you should:
options: a:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.,b:Maintain your position in the blind spot to stay hidden.,c:Keep a steady pace and let them adjust.
note: Do not remain in another vehicle's blind spot; move forward or fall back so the other driver can see you in their mirrors.

question: What does a single broken white line down the center of a lane indicate?
options: a:Lanes travel in the same direction and you may pass when safe.,b:Lanes travel in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.,c:Lanes travel in the same direction and passing is prohibited.
note: A dashed white line separates lanes moving in the same direction and indicates lane changes are permitted when safe.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medication?
options: a:The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.,b:The alcohol will help the medicine cure a cold.,c:The combination can multiply or increase the impairing effects of either the alcohol or the medication.
note: Alcohol and many medications can interact, producing greater impairment than either would alone. This increases the risk while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging from an entrance ramp onto a highway, you should generally:
options: a:Use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic and merge safely into a gap.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a large gap.,c:Enter slowly and immediately move to the left lane.,d:Enter above the speed of traffic to get ahead.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, signal, find a gap, and merge smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit sign represent?
options: a:The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions for that roadway.,b:A mere recommendation only for bad weather.,c:The exact speed you must always travel to avoid a ticket.
note: Speed limits show the maximum lawful speed under ideal conditions; when conditions are hazardous you must drive slower to be safe.

question: When an oncoming vehicle approaches at night, your headlights should be:
options: a:On the low beam setting.,b:On the high beam setting.,c:Off; use parking lights instead.
note: Do not use high beams when approaching or following another vehicle. Use low beams to reduce glare and improve safety for everyone on the road.

question: What problems can worn or bald tires cause?
options: a:Make turning more difficult.,b:Increase the likelihood of hydroplaning.,c:Increase your stopping distance.,d:All of the above
note: Tires without adequate tread increase stopping distance, reduce cornering ability, and raise the risk of hydroplaning.

question: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights and/or siren, you must:
options: a:Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop, regardless of direction.,b:Only pull over if it is following you.,c:Only pull over if it is coming from the opposite direction.
note: You must pull over to the right edge of the road and stop for an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or siren, regardless of whether it is approaching from ahead or behind.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Be sure the passing lane is clear before changing lanes.,b:Always pass on the right.,c:Flash your headlights at the vehicle ahead before passing.
note: Before passing on a multilane highway, ensure the lane you will enter is clear, signal, and change lanes safely.

question: How should you scan the road to prepare for hazards?
options: a:Continuously scan the entire roadway and both roadsides ahead and around you.,b:Stare straight ahead at the center of the road.,c:Keep both feet lightly on the brake and stare at the rearview mirror.,d:Look only as far as the car in front of you.
note: Continuously scan ahead and to the sides to identify hazards early and improve decision-making.

question: Where is parking prohibited among the listed options?
options: a:On a hill.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
note: It is unlawful to park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane; follow parking regulations and stay within 12 inches of the curb when parking on the street.

question: If you are emotionally upset (worried, angry, or crying), you should:
options: a:Start driving immediately to get it over with.,b:Take time to calm and refocus before driving.,c:Expect to drive the same as you would normally.
note: Strong emotions can distract you and impair driving ability. Take time to calm down and focus before getting behind the wheel.

question: On average, how much time does the body need to eliminate one standard alcoholic drink?
options: a:Three hours.,b:One hour.,c:Two hours.
note: On average, the body processes approximately one standard alcoholic drink per hour, though many factors affect impairment.

question: What types of drugs can affect your driving ability?
options: a:Prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal drugs—all can impair driving.,b:Only illegal drugs.,c:Only strong cold remedies.
note: Many medications, including legal prescriptions and OTC drugs, as well as illegal substances, can impair driving and increase crash risk.

question: When a transit bus is signaling to reenter traffic after a passenger stop, what is your responsibility?
options: a:Yield to the bus by changing lanes, slowing, or stopping to allow it to safely merge.,b:Honk to tell the bus driver you are there.,c:Speed up so the bus cannot merge in front of you.
note: You must yield to any transit vehicle signaling to pull back onto the main roadway after stopping to load or unload passengers; change lanes, slow, or stop to allow safe reentry.

question: What is the effect of taking drugs along with alcohol?
options: a:It decreases the risk of causing a crash.,b:It increases the risk of causing a crash.,c:It lessens alcohol's effects on driving ability.
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs (prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal) increases impairment and the risk of a crash.

question: Which of the following statements about seat belts and child restraints is correct?
options: a:You should never put an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with an active airbag.,b:An airbag can be dangerous to an infant or small child in a front-facing crash even at low speeds.,c:Ensure all passengers are properly restrained, d:All of the above
note: Children 12 and under should ride properly restrained in the rear seat. Never put a rear-facing infant in a seat with an active front airbag; always ensure all occupants are restrained.

question: What do hurricane evacuation route signs indicate?
options: a:The highway is a designated evacuation route to be used during a hurricane.,b:They are only posted during an active hurricane.,c:They are intended only for out-of-state drivers.
note: Evacuation route signs mark highways intended for use during emergency evacuations; learn their locations before an emergency occurs.

question: Anything that causes you to take your eyes off the road, hands off the wheel, or attention away from driving can:
options: a:Increase the chance of a crash.,b:Improve your driving concentration.,c:Help you react faster.
note: Distractions that divert attention, eyes, or hands from driving greatly increase crash risk.

question: When stopped at an intersection, which way should you look before proceeding?
options: a:To your left, then your right, then your left again.,b:Only to your left.,c:Only to your right.,d:Straight ahead only.
note: When stopped at an intersection, look left, then right, then left again before entering to check for pedestrians, vehicles, and other hazards.

question: What should be your first response to reduced visibility while driving?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Turn on windshield wipers first.,c:Immediately turn on high beams.
note: When visibility drops, the first action should be to reduce speed so you can safely react to hazards you may not see until later.

question: If your accelerator becomes stuck while driving, what is the correct immediate action?
options: a:Shift to neutral, apply steady braking, and pull safely off the road before turning off the engine.,b:Reach down immediately to pull up the accelerator.,c:Shift directly into park while moving.
note: Keep eyes on the road, shift into neutral, apply steady brakes, pull off the roadway safely, then turn off the engine.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when facing a steady red traffic light?
options: a:Stop before the intersection, crosswalk, or stop line.,b:Slow and proceed if clear.,c:Stop only if pedestrians are present.
note: A steady red light requires stopping at the designated stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection; proceed only when the light changes and it's safe.

question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, how should you behave?
options: a:Slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield the right-of-way.,b:Proceed normally and expect them to yield.,c:Take the right-of-way.
note: Always slow and yield to blind pedestrians using a cane or guide dog; be ready to stop to avoid injuring them.

question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must do what?
options: a:Follow the crossing guard's directions.,b:Copy the actions of surrounding vehicles regardless of the guard.,c:Assume the guard is not authorized to direct traffic.,d:Speed through if no children are visible.
note: When a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, follow the guard's directions, reduce speed if instructed, and drive with extra caution.

question: When you notice other drivers acting angrily or aggressively, what is the appropriate reaction?
options: a:Do not engage—avoid eye contact, do not react, and distance yourself.,b:Make eye contact to show you mean no harm.,c:Respond with similar hand gestures to defuse the situation.
note: If drivers are angry, avoid escalation: don't make eye contact or gestures, slow down or move away, and put physical distance between you and the aggressive driver.

question: If you encounter a flashing red traffic light at an intersection, you should:
options: a:Come to a full stop and proceed when safe.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping if clear.,c:Stop only if other cars are approaching.,d:Treat it like a yield sign.
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop, yield the right-of-way, and go only when it is safe.

question: Approximately what percentage of crashes occur within 25 miles of home?
options: a:75 percent.,b:50 percent.,c:25 percent.,d:90 percent.
note: About 75% of crashes occur within 25 miles of home, so always buckle up even for short trips.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, which driver goes first?
options: a:The first vehicle to arrive at the intersection has the right-of-way.,b:The vehicle that arrived last has the right-of-way.,c:Vehicles should proceed in numerical order of their license plates.
note: At four-way stops, the driver who arrives first goes first; if two arrive simultaneously, yield to the driver on your right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the driver behind you wants to pass, how should you respond?
options: a:Slow down to give space in front of your vehicle for the pass.,b:Speed up to prevent the pass.,c:Maintain the same speed and position.
note: When someone wishes to pass, ease off the accelerator to create room in front of your vehicle and make the pass simpler and safer.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While waiting in an intersection to finish a left turn, what should you do with your wheels?
options: a:Flash your headlights to alert drivers.,b:Signal and keep your wheels straight.,c:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left.
note: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to make a left turn so a rear-end collision will not push you into oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection to turn but are not in the correct lane, what should you do?
options: a:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.,b:Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.,c:Quickly cut across traffic to make the turn.
note: Do not make last-minute lane changes or turns; continue to the next intersection and make the turn from the appropriate lane.

question: In a city, you should look how many blocks ahead of your vehicle?
options: a:One block.,b:Two blocks.,c:Three blocks.
note: Scanning ahead two blocks in city driving helps you identify hazards earlier and react safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you start a left turn from a multilane one-way street?
options: a:The leftmost lane.,b:The middle of the intersection.,c:The right lane.,d:The lane marked for right turns only.
note: On multilane one-way streets, start left turns from the leftmost lane unless signs indicate otherwise.

question: The effect of lack of sleep on driving ability is comparable to which of the following?
options: a:The effect of being under the influence of alcohol.,b:The effect of amphetamines.,c:The effect of anger.
note: Fatigue can impair driving similar to alcohol intoxication. Long periods without sleep significantly reduce driving skills.

question: Which of the following does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:The amount you drink.,b:Your body weight.,c:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.
note: BAC depends on how much alcohol you drink, how quickly you drink it, and body weight. It is not determined by the brand or type of alcoholic beverage.

question: How is defensive driving most accurately described?
options: a:Identifying dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents.,b:Defending yourself by getting ahead of other drivers.,c:Following closely behind the vehicle ahead to control traffic.
note: Defensive driving involves anticipating hazards and taking steps to avoid conflicts and crashes.

question: Before turning the ignition on, what should you do?
options: a:Make sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.,b:Make sure all occupants, including the driver, have fastened their seat belts.,c:Make sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.,d:Make sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
note: Develop a routine: before switching on the ignition, fasten your seat belt and ensure all passengers do likewise.

question: When children are in a vehicle, what is the safest practice?
options: a:Hold them securely in an adult's lap.,b:Keep them standing on the vehicle floor.,c:Use proper child seats or restraints and never hold a child during travel.
note: Children must be properly restrained in child safety seats appropriate for their size; holding a child during travel is unsafe.

question: Which factor does NOT affect vehicle stopping distance?
options: a:Time of day.,b:Your reaction time.,c:Condition of the vehicle's brakes.,d:Roadway conditions.
note: Stopping distance depends on perception/reaction time, vehicle weight, braking system, tires, road conditions, and speed; time of day does not directly affect it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Drivers may not pass.,b:Drivers may pass or change lanes when it is safe to do so.,c:Lanes move in opposite directions.
note: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. A dashed white line may be crossed to pass or change lanes when it is safe.

question: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, what is the correct action to warn other drivers?
options: a:Sit in your car and wait for help.,b:Use your four-way flashers (hazard lights) to warn other drivers.,c:Sound your horn at passing motorists.
note: If your vehicle is disabled, move off the roadway if possible, turn on hazard flashers, and lift the hood or use other signals to alert other drivers.

question: If there are two parallel railroad tracks, what should you do after one train passes?
options: a:Assume it is safe to proceed immediately.,b:Always stop before crossing the tracks.,c:Look for another train on the adjacent track before crossing.
note: When two tracks run side by side, one train passing may hide another approaching on the other track; ensure no trains are coming on any track before crossing.

question: If involved in a serious crash, what should you do first?
options: a:Stop and assist—check for injuries and call 911 if necessary.,b:Continue driving if no one seems to notice.,c:Only call your insurance company and ignore injuries.
note: Stop your vehicle, provide aid if possible, call emergency services for injuries, and report the crash to law enforcement when required by law.

question: Which of these does NOT typically promote safe night driving?
options: a:Keep your windshield clean.,b:Be aware that tinted windows reduce nighttime visibility.,c:Rely on a flashlight while driving.
note: Carrying a flashlight is not a driving technique; the other items improve visibility and safety at night.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must use your turn signal in which situation?
options: a:Only when other traffic is present.,b:When changing lanes.,c:When pulling into traffic from a curbside parking space or alley.,d:When driving straight on a highway.
note: Turn signals should be used whenever you move left or right. Use them when changing lanes, pulling into traffic from a curbside parking space or alley, or passing another vehicle.

question: What is the most important rule for managing speed in curves?
options: a:Slow down before you enter the curve.,b:Accelerate just before entering the curve.,c:Maintain posted speed until the sharpest part of the curve.
note: Because inertia makes turning harder at speed, slow down before entering the curve to maintain control throughout the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should your car be positioned when preparing to make a right turn?
options: a:As far to the right side of the street as possible.,b:Near the center of the street.,c:Close to the left side of the street.,d:In the middle lane.
note: For right turns, position your vehicle as far to the right as possible without leaving the roadway or entering a bike lane improperly.

question: Which headlights should you use while driving in fog?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Low beam headlights.,d:Hazard lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights (not high beams) in fog, rain, or snow to improve visibility without reflecting glare back at you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, what are they signaling?
options: a:They intend to turn right.,b:They intend to turn left.,c:They are coming to a stop.
note: An upward left arm indicates a right turn in traditional hand signals; left arm straight out signals left, and arm down signals stop or slowing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a green arrow signal mean?
options: a:Traffic may proceed in the direction of the arrow although vehicles must turn in that direction.,b:The arrow is used only on one-way streets.,c:You may proceed in any direction indicated by other lanes.
note: A green arrow means traffic in the designated lane may proceed in the direction of the arrow; do so only if the way is clear.

question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?
options: a:Always — even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly or against a signal.,b:Only when the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.,c:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.,d:Only at intersections controlled by traffic lights.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway under all circumstances and take actions to avoid striking them.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection requires you to:
options: a:Stop completely and yield to other traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.,b:Slow down but not stop.,c:Proceed with caution without stopping.
note: A flashing red light has the same requirement as a stop sign: stop, then continue when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A center lane marked for special use typically allows drivers to:
options: a:Make left turns from that lane.,b:Pass slow-moving traffic.,c:Use it for through traffic.
note: Center lanes marked for left-turns are reserved for vehicles making left turns from either direction and should not be used for passing.

question: Where are roads most likely to freeze first in cold or wet conditions?
options: a:In shaded areas such as those under trees or next to buildings.,b:On flat, open stretches.,c:In areas receiving direct sun.,d:On the crest of hills only.
note: Shaded areas freeze faster and remain icy longer; take extra care on shaded sections of road in cold or wet weather.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing without gates or flashing lights, what is the correct action?
options: a:Be prepared to yield to any approaching train and do not cross until the way is clear.,b:Cross immediately and quickly.,c:Always stop before crossing even if no train is visible.
note: If no gates or signals are present, slow and be ready to yield to trains; never cross until you are sure no train is coming and you can clear the tracks.

question: When may you park or stop along the freeway shoulder?
options: a:If no part of your vehicle is on the road and there is no emergency.,b:Only in an emergency; otherwise it is prohibited.,c:If you turn on four-way flashers it is permitted.,d:Whenever you need to read a map.
note: Parking on the freeway shoulder is prohibited except in emergencies; you must not stop there for non-emergencies.

question: What is the shape of a stop sign?
options: a:Octagon.,b:Rectangle.,c:Circle.
note: Stop signs are uniquely eight-sided (octagonal) and require drivers to come to a complete stop before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, what sequence should you perform?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, check blind spot in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.,b:Check mirrors and then change lanes without signaling.,c:Signal and immediately change lanes.,d:Check mirrors, sound horn, then change lanes.
note: When changing lanes, signal, check rearview and side mirrors, look over your shoulder to check the blind spot, and change lanes only when it is safe.

question: As a pedestrian, what should you do when vehicles are approaching?
options: a:Do not enter the street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.,b:Always demand right-of-way in a crosswalk.,c:Enter the crosswalk because drivers must stop for you.
note: Pedestrians should avoid stepping into a street or crosswalk when vehicles are near; although pedestrians generally have right-of-way, a close vehicle may not have time to stop.

question: When are roads most slippery during a rainstorm?
options: a:During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.,b:After it has been raining for an hour or more.,c:The day after it rains.
note: Pavement often becomes most slippery in the first 10–15 minutes of rain because oils on the road surface mix with water, creating slick conditions, especially when hot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver is following you too closely on a multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to increase distance.,b:Move into another lane to let the car pass.,c:Slow down but stay in your lane.
note: If someone is tailgating on a multi-lane highway, change lanes to the right and let them pass to reduce risk.

question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway you should:
options: a:Check mirrors, look over your shoulder for blind spots, and signal.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Sound your horn before starting your lane change.
note: Verify the lane is clear by checking rearview and side mirrors and glancing over your shoulder for blind spots; signal before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you reduce your speed below the posted limit?
options: a:Whenever conditions (weather, visibility, road surface) make driving less than perfect.,b:Only when you see a police officer.,c:Only when entering a highway with other cars.
note: If the road is wet, slippery, visibility is poor, or any other condition makes driving unsafe, slow below the posted limit. You can be cited for driving too fast for conditions even if under the speed limit.

question: What is the proper initial step when parallel parking between two vehicles?
options: a:Pull up even with the vehicle in front of the space.,b:Turn your wheels to the left immediately.,c:Back in at full speed to clear the space quickly.
note: After selecting a spot, stop parallel to the vehicle ahead of the space, signal, check traffic, then begin your backing maneuver into the space.

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical effect of drinking alcohol?
options: a:Your reflexes slow down.,b:Your judgment of speed and distance is improved.,c:You become less alert.
note: Alcohol impairs reflexes, judgment, and alertness. It does not improve perception of speed or distance.

question: What is the purpose of a yellow-and-black diamond-shaped sign?
options: a:Warn drivers about conditions on or near the road ahead.,b:Help direct you to upcoming cities and towns.,c:Indicate a speed limit change.
note: Diamond-shaped yellow warning signs with black symbols alert drivers to upcoming roadway conditions or hazards.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:It can allow carbon monoxide into the passenger compartment, causing poisoning.,b:It only increases pollution and is not a health risk.,c:It causes a loss of hearing.,d:It reduces seat belt effectiveness.
note: A leaking exhaust can permit carbon monoxide fumes into the cabin, posing a serious poisoning risk; defective exhaust parts should be repaired.

question: What is the best way to avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.,b:Simply refuse a drink by saying you are driving.,c:Call a taxi after you have been drinking.
note: The safest approach is to decide before drinking that you will not drive; alcohol impairs judgment, so decisions made after drinking are unreliable.

question: When passing a large truck or bus, what effect should a driver of a small vehicle be ready for?
options: a:Loud noises.,b:Excess air pollution.,c:Wind gusts from the large vehicle.
note: Large vehicles can create gusts of wind that may affect the direction of smaller vehicles. Be prepared to correct your steering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning or changing lanes, when must you signal?
options: a:Always signal your intentions even if no visible traffic is present.,b:Signal only if another vehicle is present.,c:Signal only at night.,d:Signal only after initiating the maneuver.
note: Drivers must always signal when turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb to inform others of their intentions.

question: What is the only reliable way to reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Exercise.,c:Allow your body time to eliminate the alcohol.,d:Take a cold shower.
note: The only effective way to reduce BAC is to allow time for your body to eliminate the alcohol; coffee, exercise, and cold showers do not lower BAC.

question: Driving down a long or steep hill, what should you monitor?
options: a:Assume all traffic maintains a constant speed.,b:Check your mirrors for traffic building up behind you.,c:Ignore large trucks.
note: Check mirrors for approaching traffic, especially trucks that may be accelerating downhill, and be prepared to adjust speed or move over safely.

question: If another driver is passing your car, what should you do to help them complete the pass safely?
options: a:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow the passing vehicle to re-enter the lane.,b:Pull off the road immediately.,c:Signal aggressively to warn them.,d:Brake suddenly to prevent the pass.
note: When being passed, maintain steady speed or slightly reduce speed and ensure no oncoming traffic so the passing driver can return safely.

question: What describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Someone who daydreams or stares at objects off the roadway instead of scanning the road.,b:A driver who maintains eye contact with a passenger while talking.,c:Someone who looks only at the car directly ahead.
note: Avoid distractions such as daydreaming, looking at passengers or reading; keep scanning the road and mirrors regularly.

question: In winter, how do shaded areas on the road behave compared to the rest of the roadway?
options: a:They tend to freeze before and stay icy longer than other areas.,b:They freeze after the rest of the road.,c:They behave the same as the rest of the road.
note: Shaded spots are likely to freeze earlier and remain icy longer, so use extra caution on overpasses, bridges, and shaded stretches in cold weather.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering an interstate from an entrance or acceleration ramp should:
options: a:Yield to vehicles already on the interstate and merge when safe.,b:Force other vehicles to make room because they are on the ramp.,c:Assume they have right-of-way over interstate traffic.
note: When entering from a ramp, yield to traffic on the interstate and merge safely at a speed that matches traffic when possible.

question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes to the left, where should you glance?
options: a:Over your left shoulder.,b:Over your right shoulder.,c:Only at your left side mirror.
note: Look over your left shoulder into the lane you plan to enter to ensure no vehicle is in your blind spot.

question: Compared with daytime driving, driving at night is:
options: a:More dangerous because visibility is reduced and hazards are harder to see.,b:Less dangerous.,c:No different in terms of risk.
note: Night driving reduces visibility, increases glare risk, and often involves more fatigued or impaired drivers, making it more dangerous.

question: Which measures help prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Making sure your tires have good tread depth.,b:Keeping your tires properly inflated.,c:Reducing speed in rainy conditions.,d:All of the above
note: To reduce risk of hydroplaning, maintain good tire tread and pressure and reduce speed in wet conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green arrow on a signal allow drivers to do?
options: a:Turn in the arrow's direction after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Merge into the lane indicated by the arrow without yielding.,c:Stop and wait for a green circular light before turning.
note: A steady green arrow permits drivers in the proper lane to turn in the arrow's direction after yielding to any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway divided by two solid yellow lines, when are you allowed to cross them?
options: a:Only to make a left turn into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.,b:To pass another vehicle if there is no oncoming traffic.,c:Under no circumstances at all.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing but may be crossed to turn left into or out of driveways, alleys, or private roads where permitted.

question: Signs that require drivers to obey a stated instruction are called what?
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Regulatory signs (often rectangular with black/white or red/white) inform drivers of laws and rules that must be followed.

question: What do round traffic signs typically indicate?
options: a:School zones.,b:Upcoming railroad crossings.,c:No passing zones.
note: Round traffic signs warn drivers of an upcoming railroad crossing; use extra caution when approaching.
